issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) specifies checkOrderReady() as a void method, but the provided solution implements checkOrderReady() with a boolean return type. This divergence in method signature is a structural inconsistency and can confuse students about the expected API and return value semantics.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either (a) change the solution's checkOrderReady() to return void (removing the boolean return value and keeping its internal behavior), or (b) update the problem statement/UML to declare checkOrderReady() as returning boolean and document the meaning of the returned value. Preferred fix: make checkOrderReady() void to match the UML/specification.
